title: Determiners
description: Learn determiners for Grade 8: articles, demonstratives, possessives, quantifiers, some vs any, few vs a few and little vs a little — with bilingual notes, practice and tests.

topics.title: Kinds of Determiners & Quantifiers
topics.concept:
Determiners come in several groups:

  • Articles: a, an, the
  • Demonstratives: this, that, these, those
  • Possessives: my, your, his, her, its, our, their
  • Quantifiers: some, any, much, many, few, little, all, both, enough
  • Numbers: one, two, first, second
  • Distributives: each, every, either, neither

Quantifiers must match the noun type:

  • Countable: many apples, a few apples, several apples.
  • Uncountable: much water, a little water.
  • Both: some/a lot of/enough/no + either type.

topics.title: Some vs Any · Few/A Few · Little/A Little
topics.concept:
some vs any:

  • some — positive sentences, offers and requests: I have some money. Would you like some tea?
  • any — negatives and questions: I don't have any money. Is there any sugar?

few vs a few (countable):

  • few = almost none (negative idea): Few people came. (disappointing)
  • a few = some (positive idea): A few people came. (at least some)

little vs a little (uncountable):

  • little = almost none: There is little hope.
  • a little = some: There is a little hope.

examples.problem: Positive or negative meaning? Few students passed.

recap: some → positives, offers, requests; any → negatives & questions
few = almost none; a few = some (countable)
little = almost none; a little = some (uncountable)

questions.q: '___ students passed; it was a poor result.'
'We have ___ time; let's grab a coffee.'
'___ of the two boys is taller?'
questions.explanation: For two, use 'Which', and the verb is singular.

Spot the error: 'He gave me many useful informations.'
options: many useful informations → much useful information
questions.explanation: 'information' is uncountable and has no plural.

Choose the correct quantifier: 'Hardly ___ students understood the question.'
Rearrange: 'left / little / there / time / is / very'
options: There is very little time left.
There is little very time left.
Very there is little time left.
Time there is very little left.

outcomes: Name the main kinds of determiners
Use quantifiers (much, many, some, any) with the right nouns
Distinguish few / a few and little / a little

intro.en: A determiner is a word placed before a noun to show which one or how much/many: the book, my book, some books, each book. Articles, demonstratives, possessives and quantifiers are all determiners. Choosing the right one — especially with countable vs uncountable nouns — is the focus here.
intro.hi: निर्धारक (determiner) वह शब्द है जो संज्ञा से पहले आकर बताता है कि कौन-सी या कितनी: the book, my book, some books, each book। articles, demonstratives, possessives और quantifiers — सब determiners हैं। सही चुनाव — विशेषकर गणनीय बनाम अगणनीय संज्ञाओं के साथ — यही इस अध्याय का केंद्र है।

real_life.situation:
You take stock of the kitchen:

You: There's some milk but not much sugar. We have a few eggs and only a little flour. We need some bread.
real_life.why: Notice 'much sugar' / 'a little flour' (uncountable) vs 'a few eggs' (countable), and 'some' in a positive sentence. Determiners must match whether a noun can be counted — that's the whole skill.

rule_box.formula: Countable → many / a few · Uncountable → much / a little
rule_box.example: many books, much water, a lot of friends, a little time.

quick_test.q: Which determiner is used with uncountable nouns?
quick_test.explanation: 'much' is used with uncountable nouns (much water).

items.q: ______ people came; it was almost empty. (few/a few)
We have ______ time, so let's relax. (little/a little)
______ of the two roads leads to town. (Either/Both)

error_detection.sentence: There are much chairs in the hall.
error_detection.correct: There are many chairs in the hall.

error_detection.sentence: A few water is left in the bottle.
error_detection.correct: A little water is left in the bottle.

sentence_correction.wrong: Each of the students have a desk.
sentence_correction.correct: Each of the students has a desk.

rearrangement.jumbled: left / a / is / little / there / hope
rearrangement.answer: There is a little hope left.

reading.passage: The shop had little stock left after the festival. There were only a few candles and not much oil. "Do you have any lamps?" a customer asked. "I have some," the owner replied, "but each lamp is quite expensive, and few people can afford them now. Still, a little patience and the prices will fall."

questions.q: Explain the difference between 'little stock' and 'a little patience' here.
questions.answer: 'little stock' = almost no stock (negative); 'a little patience' = some patience (positive).

questions.q: Why does the customer use 'any' and the owner 'some'?
questions.answer: The customer asks a question ('any lamps?'); the owner makes a positive statement ('I have some').
'each' is a distributive determiner and takes a singular noun and verb.

speaking: I have many friends at school.

writing.prompt: Write five sentences about your school bag and lunch, using many, much, some, a few and a little correctly.
writing.example: I have many books and a few pens. There is some water and a little fruit, but not much space.

micro_quiz.explanation: Negatives use 'any'; 'much money' also fits an uncountable noun.
